title: tenant_admin can promote any member, including self, to tenant_owner via PATCH /team/members/{id}, bypassing the invite() owner-only guard
description: Verifier assessment: source-verified yes (both stacks); exploitable by any authenticated tenant_admin (holds roles.write); impact if no hidden guard exists is a vertical privilege escalation to tenant_owner, which adds billing.write, finance.write and ai.recordings that tenant_admin lacks. Rbac::ROLES includes tenant_owner. invite() blocks role=tenant_owner unless ctx.role is tenant_owner (TeamController.php ~81, team.ts ~58), but updateMember (TeamController.php ~124-152, team.ts ~89-111) only calls requirePermission roles.write, accepts any role in ROLES, does not compare the caller's role with the target or new role, and does not exclude the caller's own membership. The last-owner guard fires only when the sole owner is demoted, so it does not block promotion; it also ignores status=suspended, so a sole owner can be suspended by a tenant_admin. removeMember (team.write) lets an admin delete a non-self owner when owners>1. No policy, DB trigger or middleware checking the owner role was found. Secondary: invite() lets a tenant_admin invite finance_manager, which carries billing.write and finance.write. No code was run.
claimed_root_cause: Authorization is inconsistent across team-management endpoints. The owner-assignment restriction exists only in invite(). updateMember checks only the generic roles.write permission and never checks that a non-owner caller cannot grant, modify or suspend tenant_owner memberships or assign their own role.

trace.description: Authenticated tenant-scoped route reaching TeamController::updateMember, with no role-specific middleware.
Only requirePermission roles.write is enforced; tenant_admin holds it.
Role is validated only against Rbac::ROLES, which includes tenant_owner; no owner-caller check and no self-target check; last-owner guard ~132 only blocks demoting the sole owner.
Writes role=tenant_owner (and status) to the target membership, which can be the caller's own. Worker equivalent: api/routes/team.ts ~108.

evidence.description: invite() owner-only guard for tenant_owner, with no equivalent in updateMember.
tenant_admin has roles.write and team.write but lacks billing.write, finance.write and ai.recordings; tenant_owner has all of them.
Worker updateMember has the same missing guard.
Worker TENANT_ROLE_PERMISSIONS shows the same tenant_admin vs tenant_owner gap.

blockers: No code was executed (no PHP runtime / sandbox), so a DB trigger or middleware outside the reviewed files is not ruled out beyond a source scan that found none.
Intended-design question: whether the product intends tenant_admin to be able to grant owner; the invite() guard suggests not.

validation_plan.local: With dummy data, create a tenant with an owner and a tenant_admin. As the admin, PATCH /api/v1/team/members/{admin_membership_id} {"role":"tenant_owner"}; expect 200 and a changed role (current behavior), then call a billing.write endpoint as that user. Repeat on the Worker with a local D1 fixture. Also PATCH {"status":"suspended"} on the sole owner and POST /team/invite with role finance_manager as tenant_admin.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms no DB trigger/constraint on tenant_memberships.role in production and reviews audit_log for role changes where the actor was a tenant_admin and the new role tenant_owner.
